project.name: self-agent
project.description: Enterprise-grade AI Agent built on LangGraph, MCP, A2A, and a unified multi-protocol LLM abstraction (GLM/OpenAI/Anthropic); ships both as a coding-agent CLI and a deployable multi-user service.

nodes.name: executor.py
nodes.summary: Implements the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol executor that wraps the LangGraph agent, exposing execute and cancel operations for remote agent invocation.
nodes.languageNotes: Subclasses the a2a-sdk AgentExecutor base class; delegates to run_agent from the core graph.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: Mounts A2A JSON-RPC and REST routes onto a FastAPI application, wiring up the executor, agent card, and in-memory task store.

nodes.name: standalone.py
nodes.summary: Standalone entry point that creates a minimal FastAPI app exposing only the A2A endpoint, runnable via uvicorn with configurable host and port.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses argparse for CLI arguments and uvicorn.run() for the ASGI server.

nodes.name: registry.py
nodes.summary: Central tool registry managing tool registration, lookup, and risk classification (safe vs destructive) for the agent's tool-calling system.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Built-in agent tools including a safe AST-based arithmetic calculator, current-time lookup with timezone support, and a mock weather query.
nodes.languageNotes: The calculator uses Python's ast module to safely evaluate arithmetic expressions without eval().

nodes.name: files.py
nodes.summary: File-system tools for the agent: read, list, glob, grep, write, edit, and delete, all routed through workspace path resolution and sensitive-file guards.

nodes.name: shell.py
nodes.summary: Shell command execution tool that integrates sandbox wrapping (bubblewrap/Landlock), blocks destructive commands, and captures output with timeout handling.

nodes.name: logging.py
nodes.summary: Centralized logging configuration with OpenTelemetry trace-ID injection via a custom log filter, configurable format and log level from application settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a contextvars-based trace ID propagated from OpenTelemetry, injected into every log record via a logging.Filter subclass.

nodes.name: manager.py
nodes.summary: Unified database connection manager for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Neo4j with lazy connect/disconnect lifecycle and settings-driven backend selection.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes each backend as a lazily-initialized property; _try wrapper logs and swallows connection errors so missing backends degrade gracefully.

nodes.name: SelfAgentExecutor
nodes.summary: A2A executor that receives remote agent messages, delegates to the core run_agent function, and returns the reply as a task artifact.

nodes.name: build_agent_card
nodes.summary: Constructs the AgentCard metadata describing this agent's capabilities, skills, and endpoints for A2A discovery.

nodes.name: mount_a2a
nodes.summary: Mounts A2A JSON-RPC and REST routes onto a FastAPI app, creating the executor, request handler, and in-memory task store.

nodes.name: create_a2a_app
nodes.summary: Creates a minimal FastAPI application with logging configured and the A2A endpoint mounted.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses host/port arguments and launches the standalone A2A server via uvicorn.

nodes.name: ToolRisk
nodes.summary: Enum classifying tool risk levels (safe, destructive) used to gate which tools require user approval.

nodes.name: _risk_from_metadata
nodes.summary: Infers a ToolRisk level from a tool's metadata dictionary, falling back to safe when unspecified.

nodes.name: register_tool
nodes.summary: Registers a single tool with its risk level in the global tool registry.

nodes.name: register_tools
nodes.summary: Batch-registers multiple tools with a shared risk level by delegating to register_tool.

nodes.name: refresh_from_mcp
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the tool registry from a set of MCP-provided tools, reclassifying risk levels for each.

nodes.name: _safe_eval_node
nodes.summary: Recursively evaluates a Python AST node using a whitelist of safe arithmetic and comparison operators, rejecting anything else.

nodes.name: calculator
nodes.summary: Agent tool that safely evaluates an arithmetic expression string by parsing it to an AST and applying the safe evaluator.

nodes.name: get_current_time
nodes.summary: Agent tool that returns the current time formatted for an optional IANA timezone string.

nodes.name: get_weather
nodes.summary: Agent tool that returns mock weather data for a given city, intended as a demo placeholder tool.

nodes.name: read_file
nodes.summary: Agent tool that reads a text file within the workspace, supporting line-range slicing and blocking access to sensitive paths.

nodes.name: list_dir
nodes.summary: Agent tool that lists directory contents with file/directory type and size annotations, respecting workspace boundaries.

nodes.name: glob_files
nodes.summary: Agent tool that finds files matching a glob pattern within the workspace root.

nodes.name: grep_files
nodes.summary: Agent tool that searches file contents for a query string or regex, with optional case-insensitive and file-pattern filtering.

nodes.name: write_file
nodes.summary: Agent tool that writes content to a file within the workspace, creating parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: edit_file
nodes.summary: Agent tool that performs a string replacement edit in a file, with optional replace-all semantics.

nodes.name: delete_file
nodes.summary: Agent tool that deletes a file from the workspace after resolving and validating the path.

nodes.name: _looks_destructive
nodes.summary: Checks whether a parsed command argv matches known destructive patterns (rm -rf, mkfs, dd, etc.) and returns a reason string if so.

nodes.name: run_command
nodes.summary: Agent tool that executes a shell command inside the workspace sandbox, blocking destructive commands and capturing stdout/stderr with process-group timeout handling.

nodes.name: TraceIdFilter
nodes.summary: Logging filter that injects the current OpenTelemetry trace ID into each log record so logs can be correlated with distributed traces.

nodes.name: setup_logging
nodes.summary: Configures the root logger with a formatter, the trace-ID filter, and a log level derived from application settings.

nodes.name: DBManager
nodes.summary: Manages lazy connections to PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Neo4j backends, with graceful connect/disconnect lifecycle and per-backend error tolerance.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Conversation logging service that persists chat events to MongoDB, with graceful fallback when the database backend is unavailable.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes the agent's built-in tools over stdio or HTTP/SSE transports using the FastMCP framework.

nodes.name: local_store.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-based LangGraph checkpointer factory for local development, deriving per-workspace database paths via content hashing.

nodes.name: rate_limit.py
nodes.summary: ASGI rate-limiting middleware using Redis sliding-window counters with configurable limits and per-identity tracking.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: User profile service managing interests and preferences, backed by Neo4j graph storage with an in-memory fallback when Neo4j is unavailable.

nodes.name: sandbox.py
nodes.summary: Command sandboxing layer using Linux Landlock LSM and bubblewrap for filesystem confinement, network restriction, and private temporary directories.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ctypes to call landlock syscalls directly (landlock_create_ruleset, landlock_add_rule) and falls back to bubblewrap when Landlock is unavailable.

nodes.name: session_service.py
nodes.summary: Chat session CRUD service backed by PostgreSQL, managing session lifecycle, renaming, deletion, and thread-state cleanup.

nodes.name: stats_service.py
nodes.summary: Usage statistics service aggregating conversation events from MongoDB, with per-model token usage and cost estimation.

nodes.name: workspace.py
nodes.summary: Workspace abstraction enforcing path confinement to a root directory, with .gitignore-aware ignore matching and sensitive-file protection.

nodes.name: ConversationLogger
nodes.summary: Logs conversation events (user/assistant messages, tool calls) to a MongoDB collection, with structured event payloads and history retrieval.

nodes.name: build_mcp_server
nodes.summary: Creates a FastMCP server instance and registers all built-in agent tools as MCP tool endpoints with auto-generated JSON schemas.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that parses transport arguments and launches the MCP server over stdio or HTTP.

nodes.name: sqlite_path_for
nodes.summary: Derives a unique SQLite database path for a workspace by content-hashing its resolved root path.

nodes.name: resolve_sqlite_path
nodes.summary: Resolves the SQLite checkpointer path for the current workspace, selecting configured or computed paths.

nodes.name: create_sqlite_checkpointer
nodes.summary: Creates a LangGraph AsyncSqliteSaver checkpointer at the resolved workspace-specific database path.

nodes.name: RateLimitMiddleware
nodes.summary: ASGI middleware that enforces per-identity request rate limits using Redis sliding-window counters, returning 429 when exceeded.

nodes.name: _send_429
nodes.summary: Constructs and sends an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response with a Retry-After header.

nodes.name: _get_identity
nodes.summary: Extracts the client identity key (user ID or IP) from the ASGI scope for rate-limit bucketing.

nodes.name: ProfileService
nodes.summary: Manages user profile data (interests, preferences, attributes) via Neo4j graph queries, with an in-memory fallback dictionary when Neo4j is unavailable.

nodes.name: SandboxBackend
nodes.summary: Enum of available sandbox backends (none, bubblewrap, landlock) used for command isolation strategy selection.

nodes.name: SandboxedCommand
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the wrapped command argv, environment overrides, preexec hook, and selected backend for a sandboxed process.

nodes.name: _apply_landlock
nodes.summary: Applies Linux Landlock filesystem restrictions via ctypes syscalls, confining reads and writes to approved path sets.

nodes.name: _landlock_available
nodes.summary: Probes whether the Linux Landlock LSM is available and functional by testing the landlock_create_ruleset syscall.

nodes.name: detect_backend
nodes.summary: Detects the best available sandbox backend, preferring Landlock, then bubblewrap, falling back to none.

nodes.name: wrap_command
nodes.summary: Wraps a command argv with the selected sandbox backend, returning a SandboxedCommand with env overrides and a preexec hook.

nodes.name: _bwrap_argv
nodes.summary: Builds the bubblewrap argument list for filesystem bind-mounts, network policy, and private tmp directory setup.

nodes.name: SessionService
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL-backed service for chat session CRUD operations including listing, creation, renaming, deletion, and thread-state cleanup.

nodes.name: estimate_cost
nodes.summary: Estimates the monetary cost of an LLM call from the model name and token counts using a price lookup table.

nodes.name: StatsService
nodes.summary: Aggregates usage statistics from MongoDB conversation events, computing token counts, cost estimates, and daily usage trends.

nodes.name: WorkspaceError
nodes.summary: Custom exception raised when workspace path resolution or access validation fails.

nodes.name: Workspace
nodes.summary: Enforces path confinement to a workspace root directory with .gitignore-aware ignore matching and sensitive-file protection.

nodes.name: get_workspace
nodes.summary: Returns the process-global Workspace singleton, initializing it from settings on first access.

nodes.name: set_workspace
nodes.summary: Sets the process-global Workspace singleton to a new root path, primarily for testing.

nodes.name: context_manager.py
nodes.summary: Compresses long conversation histories by summarizing older messages via the LLM so the agent stays within token/context limits while keeping the most recent turns intact.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses LangChain SystemMessage and the project LLM client to produce a summary replacement for stale message windows.

nodes.name: compress_if_needed
nodes.summary: Checks the message count against a threshold and, when exceeded, slices off the older messages, summarizes them, and swaps in a single SystemMessage summary while preserving the recent tail.

nodes.name: _generate_summary
nodes.summary: Private helper that flattens messages into a dialog transcript and asks the LLM (via ChatRequest) to produce a concise summary string.

nodes.name: exceptions.py
nodes.summary: Defines the project-wide AppError exception hierarchy and registers FastAPI global exception handlers that convert application and unexpected errors into a uniform JSON error envelope (hiding details in production).
nodes.languageNotes: Base class carries code/status_code/details; subclasses pin specific HTTP status codes (502 for LLM, 403 for forbidden, 404 for not-found).

nodes.name: AppError
nodes.summary: Root exception for all application business errors, carrying a message, error code, HTTP status code, and optional details payload.

nodes.name: ConfigError
nodes.summary: Raised on missing or invalid configuration (e.g. an unconfigured API key); maps to HTTP 500 with code CONFIG_ERROR.

nodes.name: LLMError
nodes.summary: Wraps failures from any LLM provider call, optionally tagging the offending provider; maps to HTTP 502.

nodes.name: AgentError
nodes.summary: Signals a failure during agent execution; maps to HTTP 500 with code AGENT_ERROR.

nodes.name: ForbiddenError
nodes.summary: Indicates an authenticated user lacks permission (HTTP 403), distinct from unauthenticated 401.

nodes.name: NotFoundError
nodes.summary: Returned for missing resources (HTTP 404); deliberately used for ownership failures too, to avoid leaking the existence of a resource.

nodes.name: register_exception_handlers
nodes.summary: Installs FastAPI exception handlers for AppError (structured JSON) and the catch-all Exception handler that logs the stack and returns a dev-or-prod message.

nodes.name: memory_learner.py
nodes.summary: Part of the Hermes self-improvement loop: after each conversation it asks the LLM to extract the user's interests, preferences, and facts, then persists them via the profile and memory services.
nodes.languageNotes: Async functions; uses tenant-scoped user ids (scoped_user_id) for multi-tenant memory namespacing.

nodes.name: learn_from_conversation
nodes.summary: Sends the user message and agent reply to the LLM with an extraction prompt, parses out structured memories, and forwards them to _save_learned when content is present.

nodes.name: _parse_extraction
nodes.summary: Private helper that strips markdown code fences from LLM output and parses the remainder as JSON to recover interests/preferences/facts fields.

nodes.name: _save_learned
nodes.summary: Persists extracted memories: adds interests and preferences through the profile service and stores facts via the memory service, all under the tenant-scoped user id.

nodes.name: prompt_store.py
nodes.summary: File-backed versioned store for the agent's system prompt: tracks a current version and a full history of prompt versions with metadata (source, score, note), supporting save, list, and rollback.
nodes.languageNotes: Persists versions as JSON files under a prompts directory on disk; current pointer is a small JSON file rewritten on each save/rollback.

nodes.name: get_current_prompt
nodes.summary: Returns the currently active system prompt text, or the default when no current pointer exists.

nodes.name: get_current_version
nodes.summary: Returns the version identifier of the current system prompt.

nodes.name: save_version
nodes.summary: Writes a new prompt version to disk with its source, score, and note metadata, advances the current pointer to it, and appends to the version history file.

nodes.name: list_versions
nodes.summary: Reads all on-disk version files and returns them sorted by timestamp, capped to a limit.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: Repoints the current prompt at a previously saved version by its version id.

nodes.name: reflector.py
nodes.summary: The Hermes reflection step: pulls recent successful conversation samples, asks the LLM to critique and refine the current system prompt, scores the result, and auto-applies the new version when the score clears a configurable threshold.
nodes.languageNotes: Fetches samples from MongoDB (conversation_events collection) and writes improved prompts through prompt_store.save_version.

nodes.name: reflect
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a reflection cycle: load current prompt, gather recent samples, prompt the LLM for an improved prompt + self-score, and save_version when the score exceeds auto_apply_threshold.

nodes.name: _fetch_recent_samples
nodes.summary: Queries MongoDB for the most recent successful conversation events (those with an agent reply and no error) up to the given limit.

nodes.name: _parse_reflection
nodes.summary: Strips markdown fences from the LLM reflection output and parses it as JSON to recover the candidate prompt, score, and rationale.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the multi-protocol LLM abstraction layer: re-exports the LLMClient protocol, the get_llm_client factory, and the provider-agnostic data models so callers depend only on app.llm.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ aggregating the public surface of the llm subpackage.

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Defines LLMClient, the runtime-checkable Protocol every provider implements, exposing provider_name/default_model properties plus chat() and stream_chat() methods that all of GLM/OpenAI/Anthropic conform to.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Protocol with @runtime_checkable; stream_chat is intentionally a non-async function returning an async iterator (ChatStream) to match async-generator providers.

nodes.name: LLMClient
nodes.summary: Structural protocol contract for LLM providers: identifies the provider, exposes a default model name, and offers one-shot chat plus streaming chat methods.

nodes.name: factory.py
nodes.summary: Factory that builds the configured LLMClient implementation (GLM and OpenAI share OpenAILikeClient via OpenAI-compatible endpoints; Anthropic uses AnthropicClient), with an lru-cached singleton accessor for runtime provider switching.
nodes.languageNotes: GLM reuses OpenAILikeClient with a custom base_url; get_llm_client is @lru_cache'd for singleton reuse.

nodes.name: create_llm_client
nodes.summary: Constructs a fresh LLMClient for the requested provider, reading keys/URLs/models from settings and raising ConfigError when required credentials are missing.

nodes.name: get_llm_client
nodes.summary: Returns the cached singleton LLMClient, defaulting to the configured provider when none is specified.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Provider-agnostic Pydantic data models for the LLM layer: messages, tool calls, tool definitions, token usage, and the unified request/response/stream-chunk types that every provider converts to and from.
nodes.languageNotes: Pydantic BaseModel throughout; StreamChunk aggregates cross-chunk tool-call deltas so the final chunk carries the complete tool_calls.

nodes.name: ToolCall
nodes.summary: Represents a single tool invocation requested by the model: an id, name, and parsed arguments dict used to correlate the tool result back to the model.

nodes.name: ChatMessage
nodes.summary: Unified chat message with a role (system/user/assistant/tool), content, optional assistant tool_calls, and tool result correlation fields.

nodes.name: ToolDefinition
nodes.summary: Schema of a tool exposed to the model in the OpenAI function-calling format: name, description, and a JSON-Schema parameters object.

nodes.name: Usage
nodes.summary: Token usage counters (prompt, completion, total) returned with each response for cost and quota tracking.

nodes.name: ChatRequest
nodes.summary: Unified non-streaming chat request: messages, optional model override, sampling parameters, and optional tool definitions with a tool_choice directive.

nodes.name: ChatResponse
nodes.summary: Complete non-streaming LLM response: text content, tool calls, usage, model name, finish reason, and the raw provider payload for debugging.

nodes.name: StreamChunk
nodes.summary: Single chunk of a streamed response; the terminal chunk carries the fully aggregated tool calls and final usage/model so callers get text and tool decisions in one pass.

nodes.name: anthropic.py
nodes.summary: Anthropic LLMClient implementation: adapts the unified ChatRequest/Response models to the Anthropic Messages API, including system-message splitting, tool translation, response parsing, and streaming via the Anthropic SDK.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AsyncAnthropic; converts ChatMessage list into Anthropic's messages+system split and parses ToolUse/Text content blocks back into ChatResponse.

nodes.name: AnthropicClient
nodes.summary: LLMClient implementation for Anthropic Claude: builds the SDK client, normalizes messages/tools to Anthropic format, and implements chat() and stream_chat() returning the unified response models.

nodes.name: openai_like.py
nodes.summary: OpenAI-compatible LLMClient implementation shared by OpenAI and GLM (zhipu): translates the unified models to/from the OpenAI chat.completions API, with cross-chunk tool-call aggregation for streaming.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AsyncOpenAI with a configurable base_url so GLM's OpenAI-compatible endpoint works with zero custom logic; stream_chat accumulates tool_call deltas by index before emitting the final chunk.

nodes.name: OpenAILikeClient
nodes.summary: LLMClient implementation for OpenAI and GLM: constructs the AsyncOpenAI client, converts unified messages/tools to OpenAI format, parses responses, and streams chunks with aggregated tool calls.

nodes.name: verify_agent.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end smoke test for the agent run loop: injects a MockLLMClient into the factory cache and exercises run_agent to confirm the graph executes and the mock satisfies the LLMClient protocol.

nodes.name: MockLLMClient
nodes.summary: Test double implementing the LLMClient protocol with scripted ChatResponse replies (including a tool-call response) and a streaming adapter reused by the verify harness.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Smoke-test entry point: clears the LLM cache, registers the mock client, and runs the agent through a couple of scripted turns printing verification checkpoints.

nodes.name: verify_hermes.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end smoke test for the Hermes self-improvement loop: drives memory_learner.learn_from_conversation and exercises the prompt_store save/list/rollback lifecycle with a mock LLM.

nodes.name: HermesMockLLM
nodes.summary: Test double implementing LLMClient that returns scripted extraction responses used to drive the memory learner in the verify harness.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Smoke-test entry point that runs memory learning then saves, lists, and rolls back prompt versions, printing verification checkpoints throughout.

nodes.name: verify_phase2.py
nodes.summary: Smoke test for phase-2 subsystems: checks the skill and tool registries, MCP server build/config loading, system-prompt assembly, and a mock-driven agent run.

nodes.name: MockLLM
nodes.summary: Test double implementing LLMClient that returns scripted responses, including a tool-call turn, for the phase-2 verify harness.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Smoke-test entry point that validates skills, tools, MCP wiring, prompt assembly, and a mock agent run, printing verification checkpoints.

nodes.name: verify_stream.py
nodes.summary: Smoke test for the streaming agent path: runs stream_agent with a mock streaming LLM and collects the emitted event stream to validate streaming chunks and tool events.

nodes.name: MockStreamLLM
nodes.summary: Test double implementing LLMClient whose stream_chat yields scripted StreamChunk increments used to validate the agent's streaming path.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Smoke-test entry point that runs stream_agent with the mock client and inspects the streamed events, printing verification checkpoints.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol client that validates remote agent URLs against a configured allowlist with SSRF guard, then delegates messages via the A2A SDK and extracts text from responses.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses httpx.AsyncClient and the a2a-sdk (A2ACardResolver / A2AClient) for JSON-RPC style agent messaging.

nodes.name: upload_routes.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router for knowledge-base file uploads with extension/size validation, path-traversal-safe basename handling, async disk writes, and optional auto-ingest into the RAG service.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central pydantic-settings configuration defining all environment-driven settings (LLM providers, Postgres/Mongo/Redis/Neo4j, MCP, A2A, JWT auth, rate-limit, sandbox, storage) with derived DSN properties and a cached get_settings accessor.
nodes.languageNotes: A single Settings(BaseSettings) class holds ~70 fields; computed properties assemble async/sync Postgres DSNs and the Mongo/Redis URIs.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application factory and wiring root: the lifespan context starts the DB pool, MCP client, tool registries, memory store, compiled agent graph and A2A mount, then mounts routers, exception handlers, rate-limit and metrics middleware, and OpenTelemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the ASGI lifespan protocol (async generator) to orchestrate startup/shutdown of every subsystem; this is the uvicorn app.main:app target.

nodes.name: client.py
nodes.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) client manager that loads server definitions from the configured JSON, connects through MultiServerMCPClient, and exposes the aggregated tool set.

nodes.name: checkpointer.py
nodes.summary: LangGraph checkpointer factory selecting between SQLite, Postgres (AsyncPostgresSaver), and in-memory MemorySaver based on settings, with reset and persistence-status helpers used by observability and shutdown.

nodes.name: embeddings.py
nodes.summary: Embedding layer providing async embedding (aembed) via OpenAI-compatible clients or a deterministic hash fallback, plus provider resolution, dimension config, and startup status logging.
nodes.languageNotes: Gracefully degrades to a locale-independent hash_embed when no embedding provider is configured so the store still works without an API key.

nodes.name: pg.py
nodes.summary: Async Postgres connection pool (psycopg AsyncConnectionPool) singleton with lazy initialization, timeout-bounded open, and graceful shutdown used by the checkpointer and store.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Long-term memory store built on LangChain AsyncPostgresStore / InMemoryStore, with per-user/tenant namespacing, vector index config, and a MemoryService facade exposing add/search/list/delete operations.

nodes.name: routes.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI router exposing RAG endpoints (ingest, search, delete_kb) scoped per knowledge-base id and authenticated user, delegating to the RAG service.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Enterprise RAG service handling text chunking with overlap, per-knowledge-base namespaced storage in the memory store, vector search, and context-block assembly with XML attribute escaping for prompt injection.

nodes.name: observability.py
nodes.summary: Lightweight in-process observability: records per-path response times and request counts, exposes a metrics summary (including checkpointer persistence status), and ships an ASGI MetricsMiddleware.

nodes.name: _validate_agent_url
nodes.summary: Validates a remote agent base URL: trims it, enforces the configured A2A delegate allowlist, strips trailing slash, and blocks private/loopback IPs via DNS resolution to prevent SSRF.

nodes.name: call_remote_agent
nodes.summary: Resolves the remote agent card via A2ACardResolver, opens an A2AClient over httpx, sends a message with MessageSendParams, and returns the extracted text response.

nodes.name: _extract_text
nodes.summary: Pulls plain text out of an A2A response by walking parts across the message, parts, and result structures and joining non-empty text segments.

nodes.name: delegate_to_agent
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around call_remote_agent that logs the delegation; the public entry point used by the agent tool layer to invoke remote A2A agents.

nodes.name: upload_file
nodes.summary: Handles multipart file upload: validates extension and size, writes the bytes to the configured upload directory with a UUID-suffixed safe name, and optionally triggers RAG ingest.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: The pydantic-settings BaseSettings model that holds every environment-driven configuration knob (app, observability, LLM providers, embeddings, Postgres/Mongo/Redis/Neo4j, MCP, A2A, auth, rate-limit, sandbox, uploads) plus derived DSN/URI properties.
nodes.languageNotes: Computed properties (postgres_dsn_asyncpg, mongo_uri, redis_url, is_dev) derive connection strings from individual host/port/credential fields.

nodes.name: get_settings
nodes.summary: Cached singleton accessor (lru_cache) returning the shared Settings instance; the single entry point every module uses to read configuration.

nodes.name: lifespan
nodes.summary: ASGI lifespan context manager orchestrating startup (workspace/tools registration, DB pool, MCP client + refresh, skills, memory store, compiled agent graph, A2A mount) and graceful shutdown (disconnect, checkpointer reset, pool close, telemetry).

nodes.name: MCPClientManager
nodes.summary: Manages the MCP client lifecycle: loads the servers config file, lazily connects via MultiServerMCPClient on demand, caches the discovered tools, and supports disconnect.

nodes.name: get_checkpointer
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the LangGraph checkpointer according to storage_backend: SQLite on disk, AsyncPostgresSaver over the shared pg pool, or an in-memory MemorySaver fallback.

nodes.name: reset_checkpointer
nodes.summary: Clears the cached checkpointer singleton so the next get_checkpointer call rebuilds it; invoked during shutdown and config reload.

nodes.name: is_checkpointer_persistent
nodes.summary: Reports whether the active checkpointer survives process restart (SQLite/Postgres) versus being in-memory; surfaced through the metrics endpoint.

nodes.name: hash_embed
nodes.summary: Deterministic offline embedding fallback that hashes text characters into a fixed-dimension vector so the store remains functional without an embedding API.

nodes.name: _resolve_provider
nodes.summary: Resolves the active embedding provider and model from settings, defaulting when unset and validating against the supported provider list.

nodes.name: embedding_config
nodes.summary: Returns a consolidated embedding configuration (provider, model, dimensions, enabled flag) derived from settings and provider resolution.

nodes.name: aembed
nodes.summary: Async embedding entry point: batches texts and calls the provider client, falling back to hash_embed on misconfiguration or error.

nodes.name: log_embedding_status
nodes.summary: Logs the resolved embedding provider/model/dimensions (or a warning when falling back to hash embeddings) at store startup.

nodes.name: get_pg_pool
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and opens the shared psycopg AsyncConnectionPool from Postgres settings with a timeout, caching it module-level for reuse.

nodes.name: close_pg_pool
nodes.summary: Closes and clears the cached Postgres connection pool during application shutdown.

nodes.name: get_store
nodes.summary: Builds and caches the long-term memory store: prefers AsyncPostgresStore over the shared pool with vector index config, falling back to InMemoryStore when Postgres is unavailable.

nodes.name: user_namespace
nodes.summary: Computes the per-user (and optionally per-tenant) LangGraph store namespace tuple used to isolate memories between users.

nodes.name: MemoryService
nodes.summary: Facade over the namespaced LangGraph store providing add_memory, search_memory, get_all_memories and delete_memory operations used by the memory API routes.

nodes.name: chunk_text
nodes.summary: Splits text into overlapping chunks of a configurable size with a sliding window, dropping empty segments, prior to vector ingestion.

nodes.name: kb_namespace
nodes.summary: Computes the LangGraph store namespace tuple for a knowledge base, scoped under the tenant when multi-tenancy is enabled.

nodes.name: RagService
nodes.summary: Implements the RAG lifecycle over the memory store: ingest (chunk + embed + put), search (vector retrieval), build_context (assemble + XML-escape chunks for the prompt), and delete_kb.

nodes.name: get_metrics

nodes.name: __init__.py

nodes.name: telemetry.py
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry instrumentation: configures a TracerProvider with OTLP/Console exporters, auto-instruments FastAPI and httpx, and provides GenAI semantic-convention span helpers (llm_span, tool_span) used throughout the agent.

nodes.name: _build_system_prompt_inner
nodes.summary: Heavy-lifting context builder: runs RAG retrieval, long-term memory search, and user profile/preferences injection, then merges them into the base system prompt under individual tracing spans.

nodes.name: get_compiled_graph
nodes.summary: Lazily compiles and caches the ReAct StateGraph singleton (agent + tools nodes, conditional routing, checkpointer) -- the graph builder wired by add_node/add_edge/add_conditional_edges.

nodes.name: resume_agent
nodes.summary: Resumes a paused turn after a human-approval decision by feeding a LangGraph Command back into the streamed graph via _stream_graph.

nodes.name: stream_agent
nodes.summary: Streaming entry point used by the SSE chat endpoint: delegates to _stream_graph to yield token and step events from the compiled graph.

nodes.name: _stream_graph
nodes.summary: Core streaming engine: runs graph.astream in custom+updates mode, emits token chunks and approval interrupts, records the turn span/usage, and handles client cancellation cleanly.

nodes.name: _maybe_learn
nodes.summary: Fire-and-forget hook that triggers learn_from_conversation (Hermes evolution) when the feature is enabled in settings.

nodes.name: agent_node
nodes.summary: ReAct node: builds the chat request via the bridge, streams the LLM response token-by-token through the StreamWriter, records the GenAI span, and returns an AIMessage (text or tool_calls).

nodes.summary: Converts a list of LangChain AnyMessage (Human/AI/System/Tool) into the unified ChatMessage model, preserving tool_calls and IDs.

nodes.summary: Converts LangChain tool objects (name/description/args_schema) into the unified ToolDefinition list for the LLM request.

nodes.name: build_chat_request
nodes.summary: Assembles a unified ChatRequest (messages + tools) ready for the multi-protocol LLM client, delegating to lc_to_chat_messages and build_tool_definitions.

nodes.summary: Normalizes a human-approval decision (bool/string/dict) into a canonical accept/reject value consumed by the tools node.

nodes.name: needs_approval
nodes.summary: Returns whether a tool requires human approval based on its risk level and the configured tool_auto_approve list.

nodes.name: _run_one
nodes.summary: Executes a single tool call: enforces policy denial, triggers a LangGraph interrupt for approvals, invokes the tool asynchronously, truncates oversized output, records the tool span, and returns a ToolMessage or StateUpdate.

nodes.name: tools_node
nodes.summary: ReAct tools node: gathers tool_calls from state, runs them concurrently via asyncio.gather over _run_one, and returns ToolMessages plus any plan state updates.

nodes.name: should_use_tools
nodes.summary: Conditional-edge router returning 'tools' if the last AIMessage carries tool_calls, else 'end' -- the routing brain of the ReAct loop.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Validates and normalizes raw plan-step input into canonical {content, status} dicts, enforcing a single in_progress step and the MAX_STEPS cap.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders the plan steps as a status-icon text block (pending/in_progress/completed) for display inside the agent prompt.

nodes.name: update_plan
nodes.summary: LangChain @tool that replaces the plan in graph state via a StateUpdate; invoked by the agent between steps of a multi-step task.

nodes.name: AgentState

nodes.name: chat

nodes.name: builtin.py

nodes.name: MathSkill

nodes.name: skill

nodes.name: 001_fix_conversations_schema.sql

nodes.languageNotes: Uses IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS guards on every statement so the script is safe to re-run; the composite unique index replaces a single-column unique constraint to support multi-tenancy.

nodes.name: conversations
nodes.summary: The conversations table targeted by this migration — stores per-thread conversation state. This migration relaxes its user_id column to accept non-UUID strings and introduces tenant_id partitioning so multiple tenants can share the same thread_id without overwriting each other.

Each variable maps 1:1 to a field on app/core/config.py:Settings.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here. The README (originally in Chinese) frames Self-Agent as an enterprise AI Agent built on LangGraph 1.x, MCP, A2A, and a multi-protocol LLM abstraction covering GLM, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It documents the three delivery modes (a React web chat, a Python CLI coding agent, and direct REST access) and the five-minute quick start built around the docker-compose stack. Read it to absorb the project's purpose and the component vocabulary that the rest of this tour expands on.

tour.title: Application Composition Root
tour.description: app/main.py is the FastAPI composition root: its lifespan context is where every subsystem is born (the database pool, the MCP client, the tool and skill registries, the memory store, the compiled LangGraph, and the A2A mount) before routers, exception handlers, rate-limit and metrics middleware, and OpenTelemetry are attached. Beside it, app/core/config.py is the single pydantic-settings source of truth, where every environment variable maps one-to-one to a Settings field. Treat these two files as the map of the whole server: anything main.py imports is a subsystem you will visit in a later step.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's lifespan async context manager replaces the old on_event('startup') hooks: yield separates the setup phase (before the app serves traffic) from teardown (run on shutdown), so DB pools, MCP clients, and the compiled graph are guaranteed ready before the first request.

tour.title: Core Foundation
tour.description: These cross-cutting modules are depended on by almost everything; logging.py has the highest fan-in in the entire codebase. logging.py injects the OpenTelemetry trace ID into every log line; exceptions.py defines the AppError hierarchy and the uniform JSON error envelope that hides details in production; telemetry.py configures OTLP exporters and the GenAI semantic-convention span helpers used throughout the agent; and db/manager.py is the lazy lifecycle owner of all four databases (Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, Neo4j). They are intentionally boring and ubiquitous, which is exactly why understanding them early pays off.
tour.languageLesson: OpenTelemetry context propagation: the trace ID set by telemetry.py is captured per-log-record via a logging Filter that reads from otel's active context, so every log line in a distributed request stays correlatable to its span in Jaeger.

tour.title: The Agent Brain
tour.description: This is the heart of the project. agent/graph.py assembles the LangGraph StateGraph as a hand-written ReAct loop (agent_node to tools_node, looping, with a checkpointer) rather than the library's create_react_agent, deliberately to keep full control of the multi-protocol LLM layer from Step 5. agent/state.py defines the AgentState TypedDict (the graph's state schema) using an add_messages reducer for history and a custom replace_plan reducer for the task plan. agent/nodes/agent_node.py is the LLM-calling node: it streams tokens, opens a GenAI span, and returns either a reply or a batch of tool_calls for the next step.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph reducers: when a node returns state, each key is merged via its declared reducer rather than overwritten. add_messages appends or updates by message id; a custom reducer lets the plan field be wholesale-replaced so tools can mutate the task plan atomically.

tour.title: Multi-Protocol LLM Abstraction
tour.description: To let one agent speak to GLM, OpenAI, and Anthropic behind a single API, this layer defines a provider-agnostic contract. llm/base.py declares LLMClient as a runtime-checkable Protocol (chat and stream_chat); llm/models.py holds the unified Pydantic models (ChatRequest, ChatMessage, tool calls, usage, stream chunks) that every provider converts to and from; llm/factory.py builds and lru-caches the right client from settings (GLM and OpenAI share the OpenAI-compatible client); and providers/openai_like.py is that shared implementation, including the tricky cross-chunk aggregation of streamed tool calls. This seam is what the agent_node from Step 4 calls; it never sees a vendor SDK directly.
tour.languageLesson: typing.Protocol with @runtime_checkable verifies structural conformance via isinstance without inheritance, so a provider is 'an LLMClient' purely by having the right methods and properties; no base class coupling is required.

tour.title: Tool Execution & Safe Coding Toolkit
tour.description: When the agent decides to act, control passes to this group. tools_node.py executes the agent's tool_calls concurrently but routes destructive ones through a LangGraph interrupt so a human can approve them before they run. The built-in coding tools (files.py for read/write/edit/grep and shell.py for command execution) never touch absolute paths or a raw shell directly: workspace.py confines every path to a project root with .gitignore-aware ignore matching and sensitive-file guards, and sandbox.py wraps shell commands in Linux Landlock and bubblewrap confinement (filesystem jail, network block, private tmp). Together they are why the CLI can operate on your real disk safely.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph interrupt() suspends the graph and resumes it after human input; the persisted checkpointer state survives the pause, so an approval round-trip can even outlive a process restart. The tool registry classifies each tool's risk tier to decide which calls trigger an interrupt.

tour.title: Three-Tier Memory System
tour.description: Memory here is layered. checkpointer.py selects the LangGraph short-term state backend (MemorySaver for dev, AsyncPostgresSaver for production); this is what lets a thread pause for approval in Step 6 and resume, or be replayed. store.py is the long-term cross-session store (AsyncPostgresStore with a vector index) exposed through a MemoryService facade with per-user and tenant namespacing and semantic search. embeddings.py provides the vector embeddings (an OpenAI-compatible client or a deterministic hash fallback), and pg.py is the shared async Postgres connection pool underneath both. The agent graph injects relevant long-term memories into each turn's system context.
tour.languageLesson: pgvector extends Postgres with a vector type and ANN indexes so semantic search (ORDER BY embedding <-> query_embedding) runs in the same database that holds the relational and checkpointer state, removing the need for a separate vector database.

tour.title: MCP & A2A Protocol Integrations
tour.description: Self-Agent speaks two agent protocols, in both directions. On the MCP (Model Context Protocol) side, mcp/client.py loads external MCP server definitions from JSON and aggregates their tools into the agent's registry, while mcp/server.py exposes the agent's own built-in tools to other agents over stdio or HTTP/SSE via FastMCP. On the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) side, a2a/executor.py wraps the LangGraph agent as a remotely-invokable task, and a2a/client.py delegates messages to peer agents behind an SSRF-guarded URL allowlist. Together these let the agent both consume external capabilities and be composed into multi-agent systems.

tour.title: Hermes Self-Evolution
tour.description: Hermes is the project's self-improvement loop. memory_learner.py runs passively after each conversation: it asks the LLM to extract the user's interests, preferences, and facts, then persists them via the profile and memory services from Step 7. reflector.py is the active half: it pulls recent successful conversations, asks the LLM to critique and rewrite the current system prompt, scores the candidate, and auto-adopts the new version when the score clears a configurable threshold. prompt_store.py is the file-backed, versioned store that keeps full history so any change can be rolled back. It is async, opt-in, and every adoption is auditable.

tour.title: API & HTTP Surface
tour.description: The FastAPI HTTP layer exposes everything built so far. api/routes.py is the primary router and the highest-fan-out file in the codebase, mounting 26 endpoints across chat, memory, profile, sessions, history, evolution, and admin, including the three chat variants: blocking POST /chat, SSE POST /chat/stream for browsers, and NDJSON POST /chat/http-stream for the CLI. api/schemas.py defines the Pydantic request and response contract. Each streaming endpoint is what the agent graph's stream_agent generator feeds into, emitting token, tool_call, tool_start, tool_result, and done events.

tour.title: Authentication & Multi-Tenancy
tour.description: This is what makes the service enterprise-grade. jwt_service.py issues and verifies JWTs with bcrypt password hashing and admin-role detection. dependencies.py provides the FastAPI Depends hooks (CurrentUser resolution, admin enforcement, and owner versus anonymous access guards) that protect every endpoint from Step 10. tenant.py implements multi-tenant isolation: an unforgeable tenant_id resolved server-side from request headers namespaces every user, thread, and memory id, so tenants sharing the same database cannot see each other's data. Notably these are cross-cutting concerns layered on top; the core agent code is untouched by them.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI dependency injection (Depends) resolves per-request values like the authenticated user before the route body runs, and dependencies can themselves depend on other dependencies, so the auth chain (header to token to user to tenant) composes naturally and fails fast with a 401 or 403.

tour.title: Client Applications
tour.description: Two deliverable clients consume the service. On the web side, App.jsx is the React chat shell (auth gating, sessions, tool-step rendering, and SSE consumption) and api.js is its HTTP/SSE client, managing JWTs in localStorage and hand-parsing the SSE stream via ReadableStream. On the CLI side, selfagent_cli/main.py is the Rich-powered interactive REPL and command dispatcher, and local.py is the architectural alternative: it runs the agent in-process with no HTTP backend, presetting environment variables before any app import, registering tools, and warming the compiled graph. Local mode is what makes this a coding agent that works directly on your disk rather than just a chat server.

tour.title: Infrastructure & Data Stack
tour.description: The tour closes with what runs underneath everything. docker-compose.yml brings up the five-service stack (pgvector Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, Jaeger for tracing, and Neo4j for the user-profile graph) with health checks and persistent volumes. infra/postgres/init.sql is the schema bootstrap: it installs the pgcrypto, pg_trgm, and vector extensions and creates the tenant-scoped users and conversations tables that the memory and auth layers depend on. The .env.example template is the canonical 67-setting manifest; copy it to .env and every field flows into app/core/config.py from Step 2 to configure the entire system.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose orchestration: depends_on with healthchecks, named volumes for persistence, and container init scripts (mongo/init.js, postgres/init.sql) that auto-run on first start let the whole multi-service stack come up reproducibly with a single command.
